seed: Putting the timing strip away used to close it to NOTHING: the screen then said neither that a strip existed nor how to get it back, so the only ways were the View menu and knowing the chord, and a way back you have to already know is not a way back. It now collapses to ONE ROW across the bottom which says what is still moving and opens the strip again when it is clicked, which is what UX-PATTERNS D9 asks a bottom dock for. This walk closes the strip with its own x, reads the row, opens it again by clicking the row alone (no menu and no chord), and then checks the row states the SELECTION rather than just the strip's name when a second layer starts moving.

steps.note: nothing moves yet, so there is neither a strip nor a row: a bar of chrome saying a still picture is still is chrome for nothing.
something moves, so the strip opens on its own the first time: a surface you would have to find before you could see it is a surface nobody knows is there.

THE TEST. The x on the strip's own header puts it away, and what is left is not nothing: one row across the bottom naming the layer, what is moving on it and how long a lap is. The canvas has the rest of the room back.
and clicking that row alone brings the strip back, at the height it had, with no menu and no chord anywhere in this walk. That is the whole complaint answered.

the reason you put the strip away was to look at the picture, so the question you have while it is away is what am I still editing. The row answers THAT: it names the layer you are on, not just the words Timing.
and it keeps up: picking the other shape on the canvas changes what the row says, without opening anything.
the chord and the View menu are the same one switch as the row and the x, not a second way of doing it: it opens the very same strip.
